# roster Trademark Policy

"roster", the roster logo, and roster.dev are trademarks of roster.com, PBC ("roster"), whether registered or unregistered. The source code of roster is open source under the licenses described in [LICENSE](../LICENSE); those licenses do not grant any rights to use our trademarks.

The goal of this policy is simple: anyone should be able to say truthfully that they use, build on, or contribute to roster, and nobody should suggest an affiliation with or endorsement by roster that does not exist, or confuse users about what comes from us.

## You can, without asking

- Use and self-host roster, modified or not, for yourself or your organization, and say that you do.
- Make truthful statements such as "built on roster", "compatible with roster", "powered by roster", or "we host roster for our clients".
- Name an application or integration "X for roster" or "roster integration for X", as long as your own brand is the dominant element and you do not use our logo as your own.
- Use the name "roster" to refer to the project in articles, talks, tutorials, courses, and comparisons.
- Link to roster.dev and use unmodified screenshots of the product.

## You need our written permission to

- Use "roster" or a confusingly similar name in the name of your company, product, service, domain name, social media account, or app store listing (for example "rosterCloud" or "roster-hosting.com").
- Market a hosted, managed, or modified version of roster in a way that suggests it is an official roster offering, or is endorsed by or affiliated with roster.
- Use the roster logo as, or as part of, your own logo or branding.
- Sell merchandise bearing the roster name or logo.

## Forks

You may maintain and distribute forks of the source code under the terms of the applicable licenses. If you distribute or operate a fork publicly, give it its own name and branding. You may state truthfully that it is "a fork of roster", but do not use the roster name or logo in a way that suggests your fork is the original project.

## Questions

If you are unsure whether your use is allowed, or want to request permission, open an issue on GitHub or contact us through roster.dev.
